items.title: 61427_Happy Caldwell oral history interview
items.q: Milton Jackson lived in the same building, where Hawk lived.

ctx.x: Well, I always think too that his lungs were hard. I don't think he -- I know some nights, you know, he -- after he played about an hour, he seemed to be able to take deeper breaths and everything. Seemed as though he couldn't expand his lungs, you know, at first. You know, lungs harden as you get older.

Oh, definitely. You know, there was so many -- the last time I saw him, he was living up there with his family on 154th Street -- 151st Street, right around the Masonic Temple. So I'm up there-- I had a group up there -- 158th Street, playing for dances, club dates, and there was a big supermarket, and Hawk drive up there with his Chrysler station wagon. Hey, Hap.
